title: Probabilistic Dataset Reconstruction from Interpretable Models
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. Its focus is on quantifying information leakage from interpretable machine learning models like decision trees and rule lists.
models_tested: sklearn_DT (Heuristic decision trees based on CART)
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion. The key findings are that optimal interpretable models, compared to heuristically-built ones, are often more compact and leak less information about their training data for a given accuracy level. The paper proposes a generalized framework and metric (DistG) to quantify this information leakage for various interpretable models.
